message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020), earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards, and has been selected to the All‑NBA First Team numerous times.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at‑risk children. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows, and has been involved in various business ventures, including a partnership with Nike and a stake in the sports media company 23XI Racing.

LeBron’s impact extends beyond statistics; he is celebrated for his leadership, versatility, and longevity, consistently performing at an elite level into his late 30s.
